title: Florida Primary Underscores State’s New Identity as a Republican Juggernaut
partialText: Republicans hold every statewide elected office and have drastically swung voter registration in the state. A newly gerrymandered congressional map has added four Republican-leaning seats.

title: Searching for Answers From the Man Accused of Sabotaging Alaska’s Senate Race
partialText: Dan Sullivan, a retired schoolteacher from tiny Petersburg, Alaska, shares a name with the incumbent senator he hopes to defeat. Is he a spoiler trying to divide the Republican vote? We traveled to Alaska to find out.

title: Google Just Made It Easier for Campaigns to Send You Fund-Raising Emails
partialText: Republicans previously sued Google claiming its spam filter was biased, but the case was dismissed. The company will now allow verified campaigns to more easily bypass the spam filter.

title: Gulf Oil Giants Push to Expand Overseas Stockpiles as Iran War Drags On
partialText: Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are seeking larger oil reserves in Japan and South Korea as regional conflict threatens supply routes.

title: Bond Yields Jump and Stocks Slip as Iran Stalemate Unsettles Investors
partialText: The yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond rose to its highest level in nearly 20 years.

title: Ship Exiting the Strait of Hormuz Is Attacked
partialText: At least 17 commercial sailors have been killed in and around Iranian and Omani waters since March. Six months into the conflict, the vital waterway remains exceptionally dangerous.

title: It’s Crunchtime Again for Canada to Avoid Trump’s New Tariffs
partialText: Canada is seeking a deal to dodge further economic pain at the hands of the Trump administration on midnight Tuesday. But at what cost?

title: ABC Sues Trump Administration Over F.C.C. Threat to Its TV Licenses
partialText: The network asked a court to stop the agency from taking steps that could force ABC stations off the air and accused the F.C.C. of violating its First Amendment rights.

title: The Blackout That Could Devastate America
partialText: The power grid relies on thousands of aging, hand-built transformers. If enough fail, the blackout could last years.

title: Childhood Friends, Adopted From India, Discover They’re Sisters
partialText: Meena Geltink and Minal Tijssen were adopted from India by families in the Netherlands and grew up less than 100 miles apart.

title: Meta to Stand Trial Over Claims It Addicted Children to Social Media
partialText: California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey are taking the social media giant to trial in the first bellwether federal case over child harm.

title: Silicon Valley Executives Are Tech Fans. Just Not For Their Own Kids.
partialText: At home, moderation and restraint are the rule for tech parents. Boredom is exalted. Maybe they’re onto something.

title: OpenAI Introduces ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ as Safety Concerns Grow
partialText: The artificial intelligence start-up announced a chatbot mode that will automatically limit some conversations to better protect young users.

title: Texas Tech University Is Using A.I. to Cut Left-Leaning Content
partialText: The politician behind Texas’ conservative overhaul of higher education is now running a university system. Some say his effort to ferret out forbidden topics is a dystopian academic nightmare.

title: An A.I. Tax Boom Could Curtail America’s Debt. But Not Solve It.
partialText: The consequences of A.I. for the budget will largely hinge on whether — and to what extent — the technology reshapes the labor market.

title: Forty First Dates and Still Searching
partialText: Joseph Pascaretta has spent roughly $65,000 on high-end matchmaking services. Will it help him find the love of his life?

title: How Israel’s Financial Chokehold Is Stifling the West Bank Economy
partialText: Intensifying restrictions have hit every part of the territory’s dealings, spurring worries about whether the Palestinian Authority can remain solvent.

title: The Little-Known Link Between Dementia and Epilepsy
partialText: Doctors were stumped by his memory loss and confusion, until he met the epilepsy specialists.

title: Hayden Panettiere Grew Up in Front of the Camera. It Took a Toll.
partialText: The “Heroes” and “Nashville” star, who died Sunday at 36, endured personal struggles that were compounded by her public profile.

title: The A.I.s Are Already Out of Control
partialText: Helen Toner, who served on OpenAI’s board, hopes the recent hack by that company’s models serves as a warning.

title: Working Capital
partialText: We look into the exploding business of buy-now-pay-later loans.

title: How NASA Engineers Are Keeping the Voyagers Alive
partialText: A reworking of the spacecraft’s power systems could extend the nearly 50-year-old Voyagers’ exploration of interstellar space into the early 2030s.
